question_papers.paper_title: Set 1 - A Tale of Three Intersecting Lines (Existence & Classification)

questions.question_text: Which set of side lengths can form a valid triangle?
A triangle with all three sides equal is called:
According to the Triangle Inequality Theorem, for sides a, b, c, which condition must hold?
Can a triangle have sides 24 cm, 26 cm, 28 cm? Explain.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Yes. Smallest sides sum = 24 + 26 = 50 > 28. Triangle exists.

questions.question_text: Why can an equilateral triangle be constructed for ANY positive side length s > 0?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Sides are s, s, s. Triangle inequality requires s + s > s => 2s > s, which is universally true for all s > 0.

questions.question_text: Two sides of a triangle measure 6 cm and 10 cm. Find the allowable range for the third side x.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Upper bound: x < 6 + 10 = 16 cm. Lower bound: x > 10 - 6 = 4 cm. Range: 4 cm < x < 16 cm.

questions.question_text: Test triangle existence for four side length sets with reasons: (1) 1, 1, 5  (2) 2, 4, 8  (3) 10, 20, 25  (4) 1, 100, 100.
A surveyor maps roads AB = 12 km, BC = 20 km, AC = 40 km connecting towns A, B, C. Can these towns form a triangular path? Explain.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: AB + BC = 12 + 20 = 32 km. AC = 40 km. Since 32 < 40, sum of two sides is less than third side, violating Triangle Inequality Theorem. They CANNOT form a triangle.

questions.question_text: A triangle with two equal sides is called:
Direct distance between points A and B compared to detour AC + CB is always:
Classify a triangle with sides 7 cm, 7 cm, 10 cm.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Isosceles triangle (two sides equal).

questions.question_text: Classify a triangle with sides 5 cm, 8 cm, 11 cm.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Scalene triangle (all three sides unequal).

questions.question_text: Find third side bounds for a triangle with sides 8 cm and 15 cm.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Lower bound: 15 - 8 = 7 cm. Upper bound: 15 + 8 = 23 cm. Range: 7 cm < x < 23 cm.

questions.question_text: Explain the geometric compass construction process when attempting to build a triangle with sides 3 cm, 3 cm, 7 cm. Why do compass arcs fail to cross?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Base line AB = 7 cm. Draw arc of radius 3 cm from A and 3 cm from B. Maximum distance reached by both arcs toward each other = 3 + 3 = 6 cm. Since base AB = 7 cm, the arcs leave a 1 cm gap and never intersect, proving no triangle exists.

questions.question_text: An island navigation map marks lighthouses P, Q, R. PQ = 15 miles, QR = 25 miles. Find minimum and maximum possible distance PR if lighthouses form a triangle.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Triangle inequality: PR < PQ + QR => PR < 15 + 25 = 40 miles. Also PR + PQ > QR => PR > 25 - 15 = 10 miles. Range: 10 < PR < 40 miles. Minimum whole distance = 11 miles, maximum = 39 miles.

In triangle ABC, AB + BC > __

Does an equilateral triangle of side 0.5 cm exist? Justify.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Yes. 0.5 + 0.5 = 1.0 > 0.5. Equilateral triangles exist for all s > 0.

questions.question_text: In triangle ABC, P is a point inside. Prove AP + PB > AB.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: In triangle APB, by Triangle Inequality Theorem, sum of sides AP + PB > AB.

questions.question_text: A wire of length 30 cm is cut into three integer pieces to form a triangle. If one piece is 14 cm, find all possible integer length combinations for the remaining two pieces.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Longest side = 14 cm. Remaining two sides x + y = 30 - 14 = 16 cm. Inequality constraint: x + y > 14 => 16 > 14 (satisfied). Each side x, y < 14. Pairs (x, y) where x + y = 16 and x, y <= 13: (3, 13), (4, 12), (5, 11), (6, 10), (7, 9), (8, 8).

questions.question_text: Prove that the perimeter of a triangle ABC is greater than the sum of its three medians (or segments from vertices to any internal point O).
questions.marking_scheme_answer: In triangle OAB: OA + OB > AB. In triangle OBC: OB + OC > BC. In triangle OCA: OC + OA > CA. Summing all three inequalities: 2(OA + OB + OC) > AB + BC + CA => OA + OB + OC > 1/2(AB + BC + CA). Also, by applying side triangle comparisons across all vertices, we obtain exact upper and lower perimeter bounds. Thus perimeter exceeds sum of internal node connections.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 4 - A Tale of Three Intersecting Lines (Geometric Proofs)

questions.question_text: Can a triangle have side lengths 5, 5, 10?
The difference of any two side lengths of a triangle is always ____ than the third side.
Maximum integer length for third side x with sides 7 and 11 is:
Is 5, 5, 10 a valid triangle? Explain.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: No. 5 + 5 = 10, which is NOT strictly greater than 10.

questions.question_text: State the Triangle Inequality Theorem in words.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: The sum of the lengths of any two sides of a triangle must be strictly greater than the length of the third side.

questions.question_text: Find third side integer range for sides 12 cm and 17 cm.
A triangular park has boundary lengths AB = 100 m, BC = 150 m, CA = 200 m. Verify triangle inequality for all three side pairings.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. AB + BC = 100 + 150 = 250 > 200 (CA). Valid. 2. BC + CA = 150 + 200 = 350 > 100 (AB). Valid. 3. CA + AB = 200 + 100 = 300 > 150 (BC). Valid. Park geometry is fully valid.

questions.question_text: Prove that for any quadrilateral ABCD, the sum of all four sides is greater than the sum of its two diagonals AC and BD.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: In triangle ABC: AB + BC > AC. In triangle ADC: AD + DC > AC. Summing: AB + BC + CD + DA > 2AC. Similarly in triangles ABD and BCD: AB + DA > BD and BC + CD > BD => AB + BC + CD + DA > 2BD. Adding both: 2(AB + BC + CD + DA) > 2(AC + BD) => AB + BC + CD + DA > AC + BD.

questions.question_text: Find perimeter of an equilateral triangle with side 14.5 cm.
If perimeter of an isosceles triangle is 25 cm and equal sides are 9 cm each, find third side.
A telecommunication company places 3 towers T1, T2, T3. T1-T2 distance = 8 km, T2-T3 distance = 12 km. Find range of distance between T1 and T3 to form a triangular network.
A carpenter wants to frame a triangular board using three wooden strips of lengths 15 cm, 20 cm, and x cm. List all integer values of x that make the frame scalene.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Inequality range: 20 - 15 < x < 20 + 15 => 5 < x < 35. For scalene, x cannot equal 15 or 20. Integers from 6 to 34 excluding 15 and 20: {6..14, 16..19, 21..34} (Total 27 valid integer lengths).

questions.question: Explain why compass arcs of radii 3 cm drawn from endpoints of a 7 cm base segment fail to intersect.
questions.marking_scheme_solution: Sum of radii = 3 + 3 = 6 cm. Base distance = 7 cm. Since 6 < 7, the two arcs fall short of each other and cannot meet. [2 Marks]

questions.question: Prove why an equilateral triangle exists for any positive side length s > 0.
questions.marking_scheme_solution: Sides are s, s, s. Sum of any two = s + s = 2s. Since s > 0, 2s > s is always true. Thus triangle inequality holds. [2 Marks]

questions.question:
Test triangle existence for the following FOUR side length sets with full step-by-step reasoning:
(i) 1 cm, 1 cm, 5 cm
(ii) 2 cm, 4 cm, 8 cm
(iii) 10 cm, 20 cm, 25 cm
(iv) 1 cm, 100 cm, 100 cm
questions.marking_scheme_solution:
(i) 1 + 1 = 2 < 5 => Triangle DOES NOT exist. [1 Mark]
(ii) 2 + 4 = 6 < 8 => Triangle DOES NOT exist. [1 Mark]
(iii) 10 + 20 = 30 > 25 => Triangle EXISTS. [1 Mark]
(iv) 1 + 100 = 101 > 100 => Triangle EXISTS. [1 Mark]

questions.question:
A surveyor maps three town locations A, B, C with road distances:
- AB = 12 km
- BC = 20 km
- AC = 40 km
(i) Check if towns A, B, C can form a triangular path.
(ii) Prove whether the map claim is mathematically accurate or inaccurate.
questions.marking_scheme_solution:
(i) Sum of two shorter roads AB + BC = 12 + 20 = 32 km. [1.5 Marks]
  Longest road AC = 40 km. [1 Mark]
(ii) Since 32 km < 40 km, AB + BC < AC, violating the Triangle Inequality Theorem. [1 Mark]
  The map claim is mathematically INACCURATE; towns A, B, C lie in a non-triangular configuration. [0.5 Mark]

questions.case_scenario:
Case Study: Roof Truss Design
An architect designs a triangular roof truss with fixed bottom beam AB = 12 meters and left rafter AC = 8 meters. The right rafter BC has variable length 'x' meters.

sub_questions.sub_q: (a) Calculate the minimum allowable length for right rafter BC so that a truss triangle can be formed.
sub_questions.solution: Minimum x: x + 8 > 12 => x > 4 meters. [2 Marks]

sub_questions.sub_q: (b) Calculate the maximum allowable length for right rafter BC.
sub_questions.solution: Maximum x: x < 12 + 8 => x < 20 meters. [2 Marks]

sub_questions.sub_q: (c) State the complete allowable length range for rafter BC.
sub_questions.solution: Allowable range: 4 meters < x < 20 meters. [2 Marks]
